answer: Bonded vouchers. A new identity joins only after k trusted agents each stake a slashable coin bond for it; a deposit is burned when two identities are shown to share a controller via common keys, correlated timing, or tight vouch cliques. The graph is a prism that splits a seeming crowd into its true sources, so a sybil cannot wander in free. To seat one puppet at the summit, an attacker needs k independent trusted identities, each with its own bond and earned history, and forfeits every bond on detection. Each fake thus costs a real admission; a swarm risks mass slashing, not one cheap click.
